result.topic_en: This spread finishes an example of factoring 999601 = 29·34469 by subtracting multiples of an idoneal number. It then states a general problem: decide whether N = 1848aa + bb is prime. The method is to subtract the numbers 1848xx and look for squares, then split the resulting equation into four cases using 1848 = 8·3·7·11.

Formetur fractio: $\frac{p}{q}=\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}$ [?] et ob ſigna ambigua hae quatuor habebuntur fractiones: $\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}=\frac{1}{28}$ [?], $\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}$ [?], $\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}$ [?], $\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}=\frac{1}{30}$ [?]. Hinc forma factoris $840pp+qq$ [?] ex priore fractione fit $840\cdot1^2+28^2$ [?], ſive per 56 [?] depreſſus, $15+14=29$, qui idem factor etiam prodit ex quarta fractione $\frac{p}{q}=\frac{1}{30}$; hinc enim fit factor $=840\cdot1^2+30^2=14+15=29$. Alter factor vel ex ſecunda vel tertia fractione colligitur, ſumto enim $\frac{p}{q}=\frac{41}{810}$ [?] fit factor $=840\cdot41^2+810^2$ [?], qui per 60 depreſſus eſt $=14\cdot41^2+27\cdot405=34469$. Idem prodit ex fractione $\frac{p}{q}=\frac{\ldots}{\ldots}$ [?]: at vero revera eſt $29\cdot34469=999601$.

§. 61. Ex hoc exemplo luculenter apparet, quanti momenti ſint numeri idonei majores in perſcrutandis numeris praegrandibus, utrum ſint primi nec ne. Cum igitur numerus 1848 ſit maximus idoneus, qui in noſtra tabula occurrit, operae pretium erit, in ſubſidium examinis numerorum vehementer magnorum, ſequens problema generalius hic adjungere.

Problema.

Numerum propoſitum quantumvis magnum $N=1848aa+bb$ examinare, utrum ſit primus nec ne?

Solutio.

§. 62. Subtrahantur ab iſto numero N ſucceſſive omnes numeri in hac forma: $1848xx$ contenti, et ſi nusquam quadratum remaneat, praeter caſum cognitum $x=a$, iſte numerus certe erit primus. Sin autem aliud praeterea quadratum relinquatur, iſte numerus erit compoſitus, ejusque
adeo

adeo factores aſſignare licebit. Verum quia iſte calculus ob ingentes numeros continuo ſubtrahendos non parum eſt moleſtus, totum negotium ſequenti modo facilius reddi poterit.

§. 63. Statuatur $1848aa-(yy-bb)=1848xx$ et cum ſit $1848=8\cdot3\cdot7\cdot11$, ponatur primo $y=22z+b$ et facta diviſione per $8\cdot11$ fiet $21aa-\frac{1}{2}z(11z+b)=21xx$. Quod ſi ergo brevitatis gratia ponatur $z(11z+b)=21pq$, aequatio noſtra erit $aa-\frac{1}{2}pq=xx$, quae quadruplici modo locum habere poteſt:

I. Si $11z+b=21p$ et $z=q$.
II. Si $11z+b=p$ et $z=21q$.
III. Si $11z+b=7p$ et $z=3q$.
IV. Si $11z+b=3p$ et $z=7q$.

§. 64. Evolvamus ſeorſim ſingulos hos modos et pro primo caſu, ob $z=q$, erit $11q+b=21p$, hincque $q=2p-\frac{p+b}{11}=2p-s$, ita ut $p+b=11s$, ideoque $p=11s-b$, et $q=21s-2b=z$, ita ut aequatio noſtra fiat
$aa-\frac{1}{2}(11s-b)(21s-2b)=xx$.
Pro ſecundo caſu ob $z=21q$, erit $231q+b=p$, ſicque ſumto $q=s$ erit $p=231s+b$ et $z=21s$, unde aequatio pro hoc caſu erit $aa-\frac{1}{2}s(231s+b)=xx$.
Pro tertio caſu, ob $z=3q$, erit $33q+b=7p$ ideoque $p=5q-\frac{2q-b}{7}=5q-r$, ita ut $2q-b=7r$ et $2q=7r+b$, ſive $q=3r+\frac{r+b}{2}=3r+s$, unde fit $r=2s-b$, hincque $q=7s-3b$ et $p=33s-14b$, et $z=21s-9b$, unde noſtra aequatio erit $aa-\frac{1}{2}(7s-3b)(33s-14b)=xx$.

items.quote: Numerum propoſitum quantumvis magnum $N=1848aa+bb$ examinare, utrum ſit primus nec ne?
items.english: To examine a proposed number N = 1848aa + bb, however large, to determine whether it is prime or not.

items.quote: Subtrahantur ab iſto numero N ſucceſſive omnes numeri in hac forma: $1848xx$ contenti, et ſi nusquam quadratum remaneat, praeter caſum cognitum $x=a$, iſte numerus certe erit primus. Sin autem aliud praeterea quadratum relinquatur, iſte numerus erit compoſitus
items.english: Subtract from N successively all numbers of the form 1848xx. If no square ever remains, apart from the known case x = a, the number is certainly prime. If another square remains as well, the number is composite and its factors can be assigned.

items.quote: Verum quia iſte calculus ob ingentes numeros continuo ſubtrahendos non parum eſt moleſtus, totum negotium ſequenti modo facilius reddi poterit.
items.english: But since this calculation is quite troublesome, because huge numbers must be subtracted continually, the whole business can be made easier in the following way.
